sections.html:
Hinesville anchors Liberty County, which has grown quickly: 70,313 residents for July 2025 is 7.7 percent above the April 2020 base. The county spreads across 516.47 square miles, with 126.3 people per square mile at the 2020 count. Seven taxing areas share the county, each carrying its own proposed rate, so pin down which one your house falls in.

Owners occupy only 50.9 percent of the housing units, so moves are common and only 80.7 percent of residents stayed at one address for a year. Renters pay a median $1,246, and the typical owned home is valued at $201,500. Owners with a mortgage pay a median $1,500 a month. Builders took out 355 permits in 2025. There are 23,998 households averaging 2.70 people, with a median household income of $60,456.

A house that has been a rental raises questions about its tax history and homestead status, so settle both with the offices below before you list. Military families are a real part of the buyer pool here, and an organized tax file helps the paperwork move.

Bills go to the tax commissioner and values to the assessors, and both work out of 100 Main Street in Hinesville. The commissioner's site takes online payments, and the office still accepts them in person or by mail at Suite 1545 (ZIP 31313). Call 912-876-3389.

Assessors work from Suite 1550 at the same address and answer at 912-876-3568. Their phone menu is split this way:

  • Option 1: administration, which covers homesteads and general information.
  • Option 2: mapping, GIS and specialized assessment.
  • Option 3: personal property, including prebill mobile homes, vehicles, boats, business inventory, aircraft and commercial property.
  • Option 4: real property appraisers.

The county's Official Assessment Documents page lets you pull a property record card or a real property assessment notice by typing a parcel number, with a separate search if you do not know yours. The assessors also take email at Tax.Assessors@libertycountyga.gov.

The county commissioners proposed 19.4000 mills for the unincorporated area and lower rates inside most cities. Your bill is the final word on the rate that applies to your house.

Proposed 2026 Liberty County millage rates
Taxing areaProposed county mills
Unincorporated area19.4000
Hinesville17.3350
Flemington17.5590
Walthourville17.7745
Midway17.8746
Riceboro17.8446
Allenhurst and Gumbranch19.4000

The proposed levy change is 1.32 percent for the unincorporated area and 6.15 percent for Hinesville. Midway and Riceboro show 100 percent only because both set a city rate for the first time in 2026. FLOST, the Floating Local Option Sales Tax, collected from January to June, trims the rollback rates by about 1.6520 mills.

Rollback rates are the levels that would raise last year's revenue from the new digest: 19.1460 mills for the unincorporated area, 16.3300 for Hinesville, 17.6830 for Flemington and 18.9030 for Walthourville. Public hearings are required wherever a proposal tops its rollback rate. Ask the commissioner which rate applies to your bill.

Most notices are mailed in May, and the appeal clock is 45 days from the notice date. The notice is no bill, and the exact deadline is printed on it.

The calendar the assessors publish looks like this:

  • Homestead applications and real property returns: January 1 to April 1.
  • Prebill mobile home bills: mailed around February 1, with 45 days to appeal.
  • Annual notices of assessment: mailed in May, with 45 days to appeal.
  • Personal property returns: mailed around December 22 and returned between January 1 and April 1.

Taxes themselves are not qualifying grounds for an appeal. Owners with 10 acres or more of agricultural, forestry or environmentally sensitive land may qualify for a specialized assessment, and the mapping option on the phone menu handles that and any splitting or combining of parcels.

Expect a visit. Staff inspect a property after a homestead application, a return, an appeal, a purchase or a permit, and when it has not been seen in more than three years. They measure, photograph and note features. State code 48-5-264.1 lets appraisers go onto land outside the buildings, and they are expected to carry visible identification.

You qualify if you own the land and the home and live in it, and the application deadline is April 1 of each year. Call 912-876-3568 and press 1 to ask what documents to bring.

The state formula takes 40 percent of market value as the assessed figure and subtracts the $2,000 standard exemption before millage applies. Some counties add bigger local amounts, so ask the administration desk about Liberty. Millage differs by area, so the same exemption is worth a different sum in Hinesville than in the unincorporated area.

Your exemption follows you, and the house loses it when you sell. A buyer who will live in the property should file soon after closing, and by April 1 of the first tax year.

Find out if the year's bill is issued and paid, then settle the split at closing. The January 1 owner answers for the whole year under state rules, and a part-year owner gets nothing back.

The commissioner's online system lets you search records and pay, and a printout can serve as proof of payment for a buyer's lender. With about half of Liberty's units owner-occupied, a tenant may live in the home you are selling. If so, hand the buyer the lease and the tax status together. Call 912-876-3389 about any open balance, and have your closing attorney account for it.

Plan the order: confirm the bill is paid, request a payoff for anything open, give the buyer the exemption status in writing, and let the closing attorney handle the split. A cash buyer can close quickly, but the same tax questions still come up.

sections.h2: Before you list a Liberty County house
sections.html:
Pull your record card first. Type the parcel number into the Official Assessment Documents page, check the acreage, the building description and the owner of record, and call 912-876-3568 if anything looks wrong. Then call the commissioner at 912-876-3389 to confirm the year's bill is paid and to request a payoff for any open balance.

Put the folder together before the first showing: the latest bill, proof of payment, your last assessment notice and any appeal paperwork, and proof of your exemption. If a tenant lives in the home, add the lease. A buyer from the military community may close on a tight schedule, so having these ready keeps the closing on its date.

If the house has a mobile home on the land or other personal property, ask the assessors' personal property desk, option 3 on the phone menu, how it is billed. Staff may also visit after a purchase or a permit, so tell the buyer to expect an inspection and to keep the assessment notice that follows.

faqs.q: Who values property in Liberty County?
faqs.a: The Liberty County Assessors Office values it, at 100 Main Street, Suite 1550 in Hinesville. Call 912-876-3568 and press 4 to reach the real property appraisers.

faqs.q: When must I file a Liberty County homestead application?
faqs.a: By April 1 each year. Real property returns use the same January 1 to April 1 window.

faqs.q: Does a Liberty County assessment notice demand payment?
faqs.a: No. It explains the appraised and assessed value, and the 45 day appeal period runs from its date.

faqs.q: Where can I view my Liberty County record card?
faqs.a: Type your parcel number into the county's Official Assessment Documents page.

faqs.q: Does sales tax reduce Liberty County property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. FLOST receipts collected from January to June cut the rollback rates by about 1.6520 mills.
